blogs.title: The Dog Bite That Bit Back: Capnocytophaga canimorsus and the Mask of Sepsis
blogs.description: This post explores the deceptive clinical trajectory of Capnocytophaga canimorsus infections. We will analyze how this fastidious organism can present with fulminant sepsis and DIC that initially obscures a superimposed Thrombotic Microangiopathy (TMA). Key teaching points include recognizing the 'second hit' phenomenon where hemolysis worsens even as septic parameters improve, the limitations of standard cultures leading to diagnostic delays, and why a history of animal contact—even minor bites in immunocompetent hosts—must trigger a high index of suspicion for this specific pathogen.

blogs.title: Beyond TTP and STEC: Navigating the Diagnostic Labyrinth of Adult TMA
blogs.description: When an adult presents with MAHA, thrombocytopenia, and AKI, the reflex is often to rule out TTP and Shiga-toxin HUS. This post uses the case to illustrate the critical steps in diagnosing Complement-Mediated HUS (CM-HUS) by exclusion. We will discuss interpreting ADAMTS13 levels >10%, the pitfalls of relying on normal C3/C4 levels to rule out complement dysregulation, and the indispensable role of renal biopsy in confirming TMA when serology is equivocal. The discussion will emphasize distinguishing infection-triggered CM-HUS from primary genetic disorders.

blogs.title: The Coombs Conundrum: Avoiding the Steroid Trap in Post-Sepsis Hemolysis
blogs.description: A crucial pivot point in this case was the initial positive Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT) which led to unnecessary steroid therapy for presumed autoimmune hemolytic anemia. This post examines why DAT can yield false positives in the setting of recent transfusions, penicillin exposure, or severe inflammation. We will highlight the importance of peripheral smear review (schistocytes vs. spherocytes) and haptoglobin/LDH trends to differentiate Evans syndrome from TMA, preventing dangerous delays in initiating life-saving plasma exchange or complement inhibition.

blogs.title: Walking the Tightrope: Initiating Eculizumab in the Shadow of Active Infection
blogs.description: Terminal complement blockade is the gold standard for CM-HUS, but it creates a profound vulnerability to encapsulated bacteria—the very type causing the patient's initial sepsis. This post tackles the therapeutic dilemma of timing eculizumab initiation. We will review strategies for balancing urgent renal salvage against the risk of overwhelming post-splenectomy-like infection, including the necessity of meningococcal vaccination, antibiotic prophylaxis protocols, and criteria for determining when an infection is sufficiently controlled to safely start complement inhibitors.

blogs.title: Genotype-Negative, Phenotype-Positive: The Reality of Acquired CM-HUS
blogs.description: Conventionally, CM-HUS is associated with identifiable genetic mutations in complement regulatory proteins. However, this case demonstrates that severe, life-threatening CM-HUS can occur in patients with no detectable germline variants, driven entirely by an infectious trigger ('the second hit'). This post discusses the emerging understanding of acquired complement dysregulation, the limitations of current genetic panels, and how clinical response to eculizumab remains the ultimate diagnostic validator even when genetics are silent.
